jobDescription:

1923. SKF Purpose Statement Together, we re-imagine rotation for a better tomorrow. By creating intelligent and clean solutions for people and the planet JOB DESCRIPTION Position Title: DGM Purchase Reports To: Factory Manager Role Type: People Manager role Location: Mys ore Purpose of the role Execute operational purchasing of DM/IDM&S to support country/factories. Support the implementation of strategic sourcing results in the country/factories and promote operational efficiency in the countries. Work closely with the internal stakeholders and execute local purchasing activities. Implement contracts, agreements, and new processes. Participate in and develop efficient standardized P2P processes. Manage supplier development activities in SKF globally on demand. Manage the supplier development resources and deploy them to run supplier development projects at prioritized suppliers. Manage projects related to quality system development. Carry out local operational purchasing activities, such as issuing purchase orders and following up on orders and invoices. Enter and maintain purchasing data in purchasing data warehouses, purchasing databases, e-procurement and purchasing systems. Responsibilities
- Manager – Factory Purchase Perform local purchasing according to defined strategy and frameworks: Negotiate and sign local agreements up to a regionally defined and agreed upon value, Review purchase requisitions and identify sources of supply for spot buys, Advice internal stakeholders on procurement issues, providing support and guidance at all stages of the procurement cycle, Advise customers on modifications from original requests (if alternative, more cost efficient, or otherwise beneficial alternatives exist), Select contract/supplier to fill requisitions in accordance with defined strategy and agreements. Participate as required in global and regional strategic sourcing Projects: Provide local market data and information to global strategic sourcing teams, Validate completeness and relevance of RFI/RFP, Participate in the evaluation and selection of suppliers, Work in close collaboration with Global Category Managers, as well as end users, to ensure local acceptance and implementation of sourcing strategy, Actively participate in the validation of the sourcing strategy implementation approach, Actively participate in the implementation of new contracts, Track key performance indicators on supplier and internal customer contract compliance, Define and take corrective actions to improve contracts compliance. Drive local sourcing initiatives: Perform local sourcing activities for relatively low spend, Perform local market analysis, and define appropriate sourcing strategy, Screening, short list and select potential suppliers through a Request for Information (RFI) & Request for Proposal (RFP) process, Develop negotiation strategy and lead supplier negotiations, Work with end user and supplier in order to resolve issues, Continuously track supplier performance according to defined QCDIM, Initiate and conduct supplier evaluations and supplier audits. Support implementation of new processes and systems, QCDIM, CSR & sustainability requirements. Run their operations according to the SKF Code of Conduct, Environment Health & Safety (EHS), and Quality Policies, and work according to the SKF Quality Management System. If the operation is EHS certified, work according to the SKF EHS Management System. Purchasing Administration Activities: Perform local purchasing according to defined strategies and frameworks. Handle invoice price deviations. Release POs from special requests. Upload new suppliers in vendor master. Generate purchasing orders form approved requisitions. Process purchase orders not transacted electronically. Provide feedback to requestors if incorrectness occurs. Work with suppliers to resolve issues related to invoices, damaged/returned goods, and delivery performance. File and update agreements and relevant documentation in designated repositories, update prices and supplier information in databases etc Chase suppliers if price lists are not updated as per contractual agreements (mainly for direct material). Check all price lists received from suppliers are in line with agreements. Distribute price lists to Global Category Managers after checking for validation. Once validated, distribute them to Suppliers lists as agreed with Global Category Managers. Support to develop and implement purchasing processes and systems. Group Reporting (MMRO) KPI Updating Ariba/ Star Ariba Database updation Supplier Development Activities: Oversee developing, implementing and ensuring consistency of best practice processes for Supplier Development. The process includes making an assessment at a supplier site of lean management practices, production efficiency, quality management processes, delivery management, etc. and to define key performance gaps. Then, work with the supplier to define an improvement program to close the gaps and provide support during the execution of the program. Drive supplier development work based on input from the sourcing teams and PL/BU ’ s; guide, support, coach, train the Supplier Development engineers. SQA Activities: Can flexibly act as SQA to support Category or BU specific needs as per Global SQA directions Key Interfaces / Interactions In the Job: Suppliers Customers Engineering Function Manufacturing Group Purchasing Project Management Quality Assurance Competencies Good Technical Knowledge about engineering drawing, Manufacturing processes. Good Project Management skills. Team Management Quality system knowledge. APQP /PPAP/IATF and other quality system requirements. Cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management Problem-solving and analytical thinking Excellent communication and negotiation skills Candidate Profile: 12-15 years in supplier development, Product development, Project Management, Purchase and supply chain management. BE Mechanical (Mechanical, Industrial, Production or equivalent) (Full time). MBA, PMP and other certifications should be Preferable.

S&OP in aerospace manufacturing is a high-stakes, data-intensive process. Without a dedicated technology leader who understands how shop-floor realities translate into data models, planning programs routinely stall, and the organization operates on disconnected spreadsheets rather than a single version of the truth. In this role, you will be the single accountable owner for our S&OP technology ecosystem. Your immediate focus will be architecting and delivering internal, interim S&OP data and planning solution built on modern data infrastructure. Long-term, you will lead our enterprise migration to SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP). Critically, you will serve as a bridge between manufacturing operations and digital systems—translating complex production constraints like machine bottlenecking, multi-level Bills of Materials (BOMs), and long-horizon demand patterns into a seamless digital planning backbone. This is a build-from-the-ground-up opportunity. You will shape how our business unit plans, and your work will directly influence executive decision-making at the monthly S&OP cycle. Why This Role Exists Our business unit is building its S&OP process from the ground up. We need a dedicated technology owner who can architect the data foundation, not bolt tools onto broken processes. The broader Data & Analytics team is executing an advanced AI and analytics roadmap. Without a ring-fenced S&OP technology lead, reactive planning firefighting will consume bandwidth that must be protected for strategic initiatives. Our eventual migration to SAP IBP requires that the interim solution be built with forward-compatible data schemas and master data governance—this demands intentional architecture from day one. S&OP success in aerospace manufacturing depends on someone who can credibly speak both the language of the shop floor (routers, work centers, cycle times) and the language of enterprise data architecture (data models, integration patterns, MDM). Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
1. S&OP Data Architecture & Manufacturing Integration Capacity & Bottleneck Modeling: Architect data flows that accurately capture shop-floor realities, including work center capacities, bottleneck operations, machine efficiencies, and demonstrated run rates vs. theoretical standards. Production Data Integration: Ensure data models deeply integrate critical manufacturing primitives: complex multi-level Bills of Materials (BOMs), operational routers, step-by-step cycle times, lead times, and component availability logic. Aerospace Demand Modeling: Build and tune demand-side data feeds to handle low-volume/high-mix complexities, long-horizon backlogs (often 12–36+ months), and strict customer compliance and traceability requirements. Master Data Governance: Establish and enforce master data standards for items, work centers, BOMs, and routers to ensure data quality across the planning ecosystem.
2. Technical Strategy & Solution Delivery End-to-End Ownership: Serve as the single point of accountability for S&OP systems delivery—ensuring data availability, reconciliation, and integration across demand, supply, finance, and operations. Interim Solution Design: Design and deploy the internal interim S&OP solution using modern data architecture (e.g., Snowflake, Power BI, Streamlit, or equivalent). Ensure data schemas and governance are structurally aligned to accelerate future SAP IBP migration. SAP IBP Roadmap Ownership: Own the technical roadmap for SAP IBP adoption, including requirements definition, vendor/SI partner interaction, data migration planning, and integration architecture with the core ERP backend. System Integration: Oversee technical integration between core ERP systems (SAP S4/HANA, Infor M3, Infor XA etc, master data, inventory, open orders), advanced scheduling systems, and the S&OP planning layer.
3. Organizational Enablement & Change Management Cross-Functional Translation: Facilitate technical alignment across Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, and Sales—ensuring all functions operate from a single, validated data set through each phase of the S&OP cycle. Process-Technology Alignment: Work closely with the S&OP process owner to ensure technology design directly supports the 5-step S&OP cadence (Data Gathering, Demand Review, Supply Review, Pre-S&OP, Executive S&OP). Training & Adoption: Develop training materials, user documentation, and hands-on enablement programs to drive adoption of new S&OP tools across planning, operations, and finance teams. Bandwidth Protection: Serve as the primary technical triage point for S&OP system issues, ring-fencing the broader Data & Analytics team so they can remain focused on the core AI and advanced analytics roadmap.
4. Vendor & Partner Management SI/Vendor Governance: Manage relationships with systems integration partners, software vendors, and consultants involved in S&OP solution delivery and future SAP IBP implementation. Build vs. Buy Evaluation: Continuously evaluate build-vs-buy decisions for planning capabilities, balancing speed-to-value with long-term architectural sustainability. Candidate’s Profile: Experience: 8+ years in IT/Digitalization roles, with 3+ years explicitly focused on supply chain planning, S&OP, or Integrated Business Planning technology. ERP & Planning Systems: Hands-on experience with SAP IBP modules (Demand, Supply & Response, or S&OP) or equivalent enterprise planning platforms. Experience integrating planning systems with foundational ERP backends (SAP S/4HANA, Infor M3, XA, or equivalent tier-1 manufacturing ERPs). Data Foundations: Strong proficiency in SQL, data warehousing concepts, and master data management (MDM). Experience working with cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake) is a plus. Visualization & Prototyping: Experience building reporting layers and planning dashboards using tools like Power BI, Streamlit, or equivalent. Functional Manufacturing Expertise Deep Shop-Floor Literacy: Strong working knowledge of manufacturing execution concepts—how a router functions, how work center bottlenecks impact rough-cut capacity planning (RCCP), how component availability impacts multi-level BOM explosion, and how scheduling interacts with finite capacity. S&OP Frameworks: Thorough understanding of the S&OP process cycle and how data must step up through each phase—from granular transactional data to aggregated executive planning views. Industry Context: Experience in industrial manufacturing. Familiarity with aerospace sector dynamics (demand volatility, long lead-time components, strict traceability and compliance requirements) is highly preferred. Experience with ITAR-regulated or defense manufacturing environments and associated data handling requirements. Understanding of AI/ML applications in demand sensing, supply planning, or inventory optimization. Experience with agile delivery methods for enterprise planning projects.
